crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Aug 11: President Trump said the US will seek compensation from Iran for '50 years' of alleged damages, including deaths from 'roadside bombs and many conflicts,' after Tehran tied Hormuz reopening to US-paid war reparations and sanctions relief (Al Jazeera, Aug 11). Trump also said the US Navy has swept the Strait of Hormuz of mines and now holds '100%' control of the waterway, a claim maritime tracking data does not fully support (CNBC, Aug 11). Iran and Oman have agreed on coordinates for a temporary Hormuz shipping route - a northern lane through Iranian waters, a southern lane through Omani waters - with Iranian FM spokesman Baghaei calling talks 'progressing smoothly and constructively,' though Tehran still ties full reopening to an end to the US naval blockade. MarineTraffic data show Hormuz crossings falling from 15 on Friday to 11 Saturday to just 6 on Sunday (Al Jazeera, Aug 11). Brent is $88.05, WTI $82.49 and TTF 61.92 EUR/MWh on Aug 11. Crisis level remains 4 (High); tail raised to 35% while base falls to 10%.

todaysEvents.summary: Hormuz crossings sink to 6 amid Oman deal
todaysEvents.delta: MarineTraffic data show crossings fell from 15 Friday to 11 Saturday to just 6 Sunday; Iran and Oman agreed coordinates for a temporary Hormuz route, but Tehran ties full reopening to ending the US naval blockade (Al Jazeera, Aug 11).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A signed Iran-Oman framework restores non-discriminatory, fee-free transit and traffic rebuilds gradually; Iran and Oman have agreed coordinates for a temporary route, but Trump's new demand for '50 years' of reparations and Iran's insistence on a blockade end and sanctions relief make a near-term signed full reopening unlikely (Al Jazeera/CNBC, Aug 11). Brent moves toward $75-85 as the risk premium eases, while Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: No workable full-reopening agreement emerges: Iran holds to its reparations and sanctions-relief demands, Trump counter-demands compensation from Iran instead, and Hormuz traffic keeps thinning - MarineTraffic shows crossings falling from 15 Friday to just 6 Sunday (Al Jazeera, Aug 11). Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Iran's and the US's compensation demands harden into an unresolved standoff, Trump's claim of '100%' Hormuz control provokes an Iranian response, and the Iran-Oman interim-route talks collapse, driving a renewed full closure of Hormuz and spillover into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu as Gulf cargoes become inaccessible.
